headline: Anthropic will ban users who are cruel to Claude
dek: Warnings, suspension and termination for persistent hostility, and a split reaction, per Olhar Digital and Canaltech.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Penalties for hostile users
body: Anthropic revised Claude's usage policy to allow penalties for users who treat the chatbot in an abusive or cruel way, persistently and without need. It takes effect on November 12 (Olhar Digital, Canaltech).
Sanctions range from warnings to limited functionality, suspended accounts or full termination. Canaltech reports the update was disclosed on Thursday, October 8, and covers only extreme cases.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Where the line falls
s3.body: Ordinary complaints and testing stay outside the rule (Olhar Digital, Canaltech).

points.t: Complaints about performance, disagreement, dark creative writing and security research testing (Olhar Digital, Canaltech).
Expected to rely mainly on Claude, which can already end a chat when abusive messages ignore attempts to redirect (Canaltech).
Anthropic has not detailed the criteria separating abuse from ordinary frustration (Olhar Digital).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: A dispute over machines and suffering
body: Box CEO Aaron Levie called it a reasonable precaution: training future models on rude interactions could shape how they behave. Investor Bill Gurley asked whether it signals customer chats are used for training, which Anthropic does not confirm (Olhar Digital).
Critics said the rule gives software human traits. Spellbook CEO Scott Stevenson warned that assuming AI empathy without proof could expand its influence over people (Olhar Digital).

stat.cap: when the revised policy takes effect (Canaltech)

items.t: The policy takes effect, with accounts open to limits, suspension or closure (Olhar Digital, Canaltech).
Teams building on Claude outside the US get a new compliance detail to track (Olhar Digital).
No public criteria yet for what counts as abuse; Lachlan Phillips suggested Claude ignore insults (Olhar Digital).

caption.hook: Anthropic will ban users who are persistently cruel to Claude, under a revised usage policy effective November 12.
body: Canaltech notes Anthropic tested a narrower version in August 2025, when Claude Opus 4 and 4.1 gained the ability to end conversations judged extremely harmful. Until now, that tool was used only in exceptional situations.

Olhar Digital reports Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman answered the news with a melting-face emoji, and recalls Sam Altman defending the processing cost of polite chatbot messages. The same revision also bars use of Claude in disinformation, election interference, unauthorized surveillance and weapons development.
